Activate.description:
Activate Host control for a session with exactly these operations, or change an active
one's scope to them. Each call that takes effect is a new generation.

ms.description:
Milliseconds worked in that hour, summed over sessions (more than an hour when several
agents worked at once).

ActiveTime.description: The time agents worked, by UTC hour, so a frontend can group it into its own local days.

hours.description: Ascending; hours without work are left out.

oneOf.description: What the person already has: what an Apply would bring.

hint.description: What to type after the command, when it takes free text.

AgentDiscover.description:
Find an installed agent's directories (`_sill/agents.discovered`), as proposals for its
`home_paths`. Without `method_id`: one first start in a throwaway jail with an empty home.
With it: that login method run on the daemon host with an empty home, as host logins are;
what it wrote is proposed and copied into the agent's sill-owned home. Declares nothing.

operation_id.description: Durable retry identity, scoped to this daemon store.
Durable retry identity, scoped to this daemon store.

AgentResetDone.description:
A reset: the agent's running sessions stopped first (a running agent holds its login and writes
to its home), then its sill-owned home, its ghost sessions' copies and its saved API keys
removed. The install and its definition stay: it starts as a fresh install does.

stopped.description: Sessions stopped; their conversations stay and start again when used.

AgentSettings.description:
An agent's adjustable settings as sill stores them (SPEC §3.2): per session (what that session
runs with) and per agent type (the default a new session starts from).

live.description:
The running session has the host now (a live grant its proxy reads per connection): no
restart is needed. False from older daemons, and for a wildcard, which only a restart
applies.

Answer.description:
Open in the schema because questions carry it in results and events; the daemon still refuses
unknown fields in `questions.answer` (requests are strict).

oneOf.description: Immutable inline data; the daemon validates decoded length before acceptance.
Immutable uploaded object scoped to this session.

api_key.description:
The method takes an API key the person types: the provider the agent names (`google`,
`openai`), empty when it names none. Send it with `authenticate`'s `api_key`.

AuthMethodInfo.description: A login method the agent offered at `initialize`.

Brief.description: Active Host control on a session record, for a window-level indication of every such session.

path.description: Exact daemon-host path, for review; never accepted as deletion input.

CancellationRequested.description: Cancellation acknowledges a request, never proof that the agent stopped.

discarded.description: A Discard's record, for its Undo.

workspace.description: Absent when the workspace's folder was freed (its session ended with nothing left).

CommandKey.description: A command running in the jail, by its root's pid there (`JailProcesses::commands`).

type.description:
text, thought, plan_entry, image (`mime` + `upload_id` or `omitted`), message_metadata,
extension, or a future display type. Show unknown types by `text` or skip them; never fail.

oneOf.description:
`api_key`: for a method marked `api_key`. The daemon keeps it where the agent's jail cannot
read it and answers the agent's next login request with it; it is never journaled.

workspaces.description:
Work in workspaces for the session's pinned repositories (docs/parallel-coding.md §12);
absent follows Settings → Automatic workspaces. Needs `sill.workspaces`.

options.description:
Empty when no session of this agent has reported its options here yet: it then reviews
as it starts.

CrosscheckCurrent.description: A workspace's review, when it has one.

activity.description: Its latest steps, one line each, the latest last.

summary.description: Its assessment in at most three sentences.

detail.description: The Reviewer's explanation: what is expected, what happens, how it knows.

CrosscheckReviewer.description:
Who reviews: an agent and that agent's own options. Its options are the Reviewer's alone: they
do not change what the person's ordinary sessions of that agent start with.

name.description: What the person calls it; the agent's id when they gave it no name.

options.description:
Option id → value id for a choice, `true`/`false` for a switch (the ids of
`SessionControls::options`). An option left out stays as the agent starts with it.

CrosscheckReviewers.description: The Reviewers setting and what can be chosen for it.

agents.description: Every agent that can review, with its options as its latest session reported them.

reviewers.description:
The saved Reviewers, the one a review uses first. Empty: none was chosen, and a review is
done by an agent other than the session's own when there is one.

base.description:
The commit the review compares against: where the work leaves the person's checkout, so
the review covers what an Apply would bring and nothing else.

created_at.description: Unix seconds, as a decimal string.

problems.description: What they found, the most important first. Empty on a complete review: no problems found.

reviewers.description: Who reviewed. One in this version.

session_id.description: The session whose work it is.

stale.description: The workspace's files are no longer the ones reviewed.

state.description:
`capturing`, `reviewing`, `complete` or `failed`. Only `complete` is a review; `failed`
says why in `detail`.

state_tree.description: The reviewed files as a Git tree, uncommitted work included (`Detail::state_tree`).

operation_id.description:
Chosen by the frontend for this press of the button: a repeated start with it answers
with the review it started and starts nothing.

cwd.description: Host terminals only: a jail's working directory is not visible from the host.

journal.description: Session logs are journald streams (`journalctl --user -t sill-<id>`), else files.

launcher.description: The session launcher the daemon found (`launcher::describe`).

limits.description: Sessions get resource limits (a cgroup root was found).

mode.description: `unit` (socket-activated systemd user service) or `direct` (spawned by its first client).

sessions.description: Sessions in the store, and how many of them have a live jail.

Definition.description:
An agent definition: a result of `agents.get`/`agents.list` and the params of `agents.save`.
Open in the schema because it is a result too; the daemon still refuses unknown fields in
`agents.save` (requests are strict).

experimental_acp_v2.description: Explicit opt-in to the experimental ACP v2 adapter; ACP v1 remains the default.

since.description: The revision the frontend shows: when the desktop still looks so, nothing is encoded.

DesktopFrame.description:
A frame of a session's test desktop, taken by the daemon (`_sill/desktop.capture`). The PNG
itself is read with `_sill/desktop.read` while it is the latest.

changed.description: False when `since` named this picture: there is nothing new to read.

revision.description: The SHA-256 of the picture's pixels: an unchanged desktop has the same revision.

size.description: The PNG's length in bytes (decimal); 0 when not `changed`.

width.description: The picture's size in pixels; the desktop's own size is this divided by `scale`.

checkout_only.description:
The person's own uncommitted files in the checkout that the workspace does not have: a
workspace starts from HEAD (docs/parallel-coding.md §5).

files.description:
What an Apply would bring, path by path, committed and uncommitted alike, sorted by path:
`summary`'s `files`, `added` and `removed` are their count and sums.

needs_rebase.description: The checkout moved past what the workspace started from: Apply rebases first (prepare).

state_tree.description:
The workspace's whole state, committed or not, as a Git tree id: the same before and after
its uncommitted work is committed, so a frontend that asked the agent to commit can tell
that nothing else changed before it applies what the person saw.

path.description:
Only this path's diff: a path below the workspace's `source`, as `FileChange.path` gives
it. Absent: the whole diff.

truncated.description: The diff exceeded 4 MiB and was cut there.

Discarded.description: Work the person discarded, kept for Undo until `until`.

Discovery.description: What the last discovery run found for an agent.

auth_methods.description: The login methods the agent offers.

login_files.description:
Files that login wrote under the proposed directories, relative to the home: candidates
for `login_files`.

login_method.description:
Set when the proposals come from a login with this method (`_sill/agents.discover` with
`method_id`): the login's files are already in the agent's sill-owned home.

note.description: What went wrong on the way, when the probe could not complete (shown with the result).

available.description: Bytes available to this user (excludes reserved filesystem blocks).

DomainData.description:
Public domain errors preserve unknown codes. Clients must not retry mutations on an
unfamiliar error, timeout or disconnection.

DomainDetails.description:
`details` by code. Only the codes listed in [`detail_codes`] carry details; for those, the
record shape is fixed by sfp/1 and may only gain optional fields. Clients ignore unknown fields.

FileChange.description:
One path an Apply would change. A rename is its two paths, one deleted and one added, so each
path's own diff (`workspaces.diff` with `path`) says the same as its entry here.

added.description: Lines, as decimal strings; both `0` for a binary file.

path.description: The path in the repository as the person knows it (below the workspace's `source`).

FileLines.description: One changed file's lines; none for a binary file, or a new one that is too large.

kind.description: choice, choices, text, boolean, number. Unknown types cannot be answered.

HomePath.description: Exact persistent locations; absence of home_paths means setup is required.

HostPath.description: Exact bytes name a path on the daemon host. Display text is never operational.

HostStream.description:
One-use token: claim on a new transport within 60 seconds. No control handshake on that
transport. Port bytes are raw; progress streams are newline-delimited Progress objects.

IncompatibleDetails.description: `incompatible`: the protocol identities the daemon supports. Always present.

InvalidStateDetails.description:
`invalid_state` (with `sill.workspaces`): why a workspace operation cannot run, as a stable
reason (`stale_revision`, `source_overlap`, `submodules`…), and the files involved.

kind.description:
user, agent, thought, tool, note, notice, plan. A plan's content is one `plan_entry`
block per step (`status`, `priority`); a notice's `severity` is on its text block.

ItemPatch.description:
Mutable fields replace the whole named field; omitted fields remain unchanged.
Null is invalid here; a tool cannot be cleared or turned into another item kind.

count.description: Processes in its tree, itself included.

name.description: The managed process's name, for a service started with `sill-proc`.

pid.description: The pid in the jail's own namespace.

port.description: A port it listens on, the lowest when several.

JailProcesses.description:
What runs in a session's jail now (docs/jail-processes.md), as sill sees it from outside the
agent. Empty when the session's jail is not running.

commands.description: Programs the agent started that are running now, each the root of its own tree.

services.description: Long-running programs: managed processes (`sill-proc`) and anything listening on a port.

token.description: Present for a newly started job only. Repeated requests recover the receipt, not output.

Keep.description: Keep (or stop keeping) a bridge-launched host process running after Host control ends.

name.description: The process's name in the process list (`host:<id>`).

LimitDetails.description:
`limit_exceeded`: which kind of bound was hit, so a client knows what could succeed instead.
Always present.

maximum.description: The bound, in the unit the message names (bytes, items, objects…), where it is a number.

LimitScope.description: What a client can do about a `limit_exceeded`.

oneOf.description: The request itself is too large or names too many items: send less.
The response would be too large: ask for a smaller page.
One stored record is too large for this method; paging cannot help.

A daemon resource is full (connections, jobs, snapshots, receipts, pins…): release one
or wait. Repeating the same request unchanged fails again until something is released.

session_id.description: Omit to list global pins; a session ID lists only that session's own pins.
Only this session's terminals; none lists every terminal.

details.description:
Each workspace's current state, one look at the daemon: absent for a workspace whose folder
or repository is gone.

discarded.description: Discarded work still undoable (first page only).

cwd.description: In the jail's namespace for a session terminal, on the daemon host otherwise.

label.description: The frontend's own name for the terminal, so it can find it again (at most 128 bytes).

session_id.description: The session whose jail runs the terminal; none runs it on the daemon's host.

Operation.description: A durable receipt survives stream loss and daemon restart. Unknown never authorizes replay.

unreadable.description:
Sessions whose writes could not be listed, with why (a launch recorded by an older Sill,
say); on the first page only. The rest of the listing is whole.

PermissionChoice.description: Remember a capability choice for one session; `enabled: null` returns to the policy default.

PermissionState.description: Capability defaults and ceilings, evaluated against this view's resolved policy.

blocked.description: The remembered choice could not take effect within this view's limits (see `reason`).

requested.description: The session's remembered choice; null follows the policy default.

source.description: `session` when an applied session choice decides the state, otherwise `policy`.

PermissionsChanged.description: The next build after a permission change. Preview is prospective, never enforcement evidence.

restart_required.description: The running jail does not have the new state; a restart builds it.

Pinned.description: `pins.add`'s result: the canonical path pinned (open, unlike the request).

text.description: A complete policy's text, transferred from the client.

snapshot.description: Older or never-started sessions may have no retained launch snapshot.

PolicyView.description: Policy inspection always identifies its view; previews are never evidence of enforcement.

filesystem.description: Exact filesystem rules; None means no launch evidence was recorded.

session_hosts.description:
The session's remembered host approvals as this view resolves them. A launch snapshot
lists those its build consulted; hosts approved later reach the running proxy live.

conflicts.description: The rebase stopped on these files: resolve them in the workspace or abort.

needs_rebase.description: The result still does not descend from the checkout (the rebase stopped or could not run).

kept.description: A host process marked to keep running after Host control ends.

location.description:
`jail` (the shim's managed processes) or `host` (launched on this machine through Host
control; such a name begins with `host:`).

Progress.description:
Login/install progress, at most 16 KiB of UTF-8 per text/message field. Exactly one terminal
event (`completed` or `failed`) establishes the outcome; EOF alone leaves it unknown.

oneOf.description:
A login page for the frontend to open in the person's browser (capability
`sill.login_browser`); the daemon opens none. `callback_port`: the daemon host's loopback
port the page redirects to, which a frontend on another machine relays with
`_sill/streams.login_callback`.

Proposal.description:
A path an agent created under a fresh home on its first start: a proposal for its `home_paths`
(`_sill/agents.discovered`; docs/agent-directories.md "Directory setup by probe").

initial_content.description: A file: what the agent wrote, when small text; the file's initial content if declared.

on_host.description:
The same path exists in the person's real home on the daemon host: owning it hides the
host's copy from this agent.

Provider.description:
A provider record: a result of `providers.list` and part of the params of `providers.save`.
Open in the schema because it is a result too; the daemon refuses unknown fields in a save.

base_url.description: `http(s)://host[:port][/path]`. Loopback is refused: in a jail it is the jail's own.

default_model.description: One of `models`: what a session starts with unless the person picked another.

model_limits.description: Optional per-model token budgets. Only models in `models` may have entries.

models.description: Model ids offered to agents, as the endpoint names them.

oneOf.description: OpenAI-compatible: `/chat/completions` and `/models` under the base URL.

ProviderDetectLimits.description: Read Ollama's active context allocation without loading or changing a model.

context.description: Active allocation from /api/ps, not the model's theoretical maximum.

endpoint.description: The one `host:port` sessions are allowed to reach for it.

has_key.description: A key is saved for it. The key itself is never returned.

clear_key.description: Forget the saved key (ignored when `key` is given).

key.description: Replaces the saved key. Absent: the saved key stays.
The key to try. Absent: the key saved for `provider_id`, when that is given.

models.description: The endpoint's model ids, sorted; at most 2000.

agents.description:
Registry ids of the agents the daemon can hand providers to (it has a translation for
them), installed or not.

subject.description: Display-only permission subject. Unknown fields never imply an authorization decision.

install_kind.description: Installation facts from the daemon's platform; frontends never derive these locally.

allow_unreviewed.description: Required for an entry from the unreviewed live index.

operation_id.description: Durable retry identity, scoped to this daemon store.

after.description: Exclusive entry ID boundary; pages are live, not a frozen snapshot.

limit.description: 1–128 entries, default 64. Each entry has at most one newer version.

fetched_at.description: Decimal Unix seconds when the live index was fetched, or null if never fetched.

Revision.description: What the person saw: Apply and Discard name it, and a different current one is refused.

destination_branch.description: The checkout's branch an Apply moves, and its tip when this revision was taken.

worktree.description: A fingerprint of the uncommitted state; empty when clean.

SavedHost.description: An agent-wide network default saved deliberately; it changes no existing session.

Secret.description: A secret the person typed (an API key): serialized as its string, never shown by `Debug`.

active_ms.description:
The session state's `active_ms` and `active_since_ms` (the time the agent worked), so a
frontend that has not attached shows the same time as one that has.

created_at.description: Unix seconds, encoded as decimal strings.

host_control.description:
Active Host control (docs/permission-modes.md): its generation and operations; absent
otherwise. For the window-level indication naming every such session.

name.description: Human-editable session name, initially generated; independent of the summary title.

policy_changed.description:
The session's policy file changed after its running jail was built: stop and start the
session to apply it. False when the session is not running.

status.description: loading, restoring, ready, or failed. Values remain the last confirmed snapshot while restoring.

SessionHostGrant.description: A host approved for this session alone (Allow), remembered across builds.

applied.description:
In this view's resolved allow-list. False when the view's limits leave it out (offline,
or no additional hosts allowed): it stays remembered and applies again when they go.

reason.description: Why it is not applied; empty when it is.

active_ms.description: Completed working intervals, in milliseconds. Waiting and idle time are excluded.

active_since_ms.description: Unix milliseconds at the start of the current working interval.

activity.description: idle, working, waiting, unknown. Unknown must never be interpreted as idle.

agent_title.description: The name the agent gave the session, if any (sill's own title is `title`).

background.description: None means background activity is unknown, not empty.

commands.description: Slash commands the agent offers now; empty when it offers none or never said.

summarizing.description:
The turn running is sill's own summary turn: `checkpoint` (Summarize now) or `end` (the
session's closing summary); None for the agent's ordinary work and when nothing runs.

SessionView.description: A session's pinned repositories as its jail has them: each a workspace, or live with why.

details.description:
Each workspace's current state, one look at the daemon: absent for a workspace whose folder
or repository is gone.

live.description: Repositories the session pins live although it works in workspaces: the reason.

workspaces_mode.description: True when the session works in workspaces (Automatic workspaces, or chosen at its start).

Settings.description: A result: open to fields added later (clients ignore unknown fields in what the daemon sends).

fragment.description:
A large record's JSON is delivered in consecutive UTF-8 fragments. No ordinary
records are interleaved. Concatenate through `last` before decoding the record.

StaleAnswerDetails.description: `stale_answer`: the question as currently resolved. Always present.

displaying.description: Connections displaying this session's control; the activation ends when the last goes.

ended.description: Why and when the last activation ended, until the next one.

forbidden.description: The session policy's ban, when it forbids Host control.

generation.description:
Counts every activation and scope change of this session since the daemon started; 0
before the first. Actions carry the generation they were made under; a stale one is refused.

since.description: Unix seconds, decimal, of the current activation.

Stream.description: A one-use byte-stream token (docs/protocol.md, byte streams).

purpose.description:
A prompt a frontend wrote for the person rather than one they typed: `commit` (Apply's
request to commit a workspace) or `crosscheck` (the request to fix what a Crosscheck
found). Null or absent for the person's own words; other values are refused. Carried to the submission and to the turn it starts.

files.description:
When asked for: the changed files in the order `repos.status` lists them, the first ones
only when `truncated`.

Summary2.description:
What is not applied yet: the workspace against what the person already has. Line counts are
decimal strings.

uncommitted.description:
Uncommitted paths, untracked included. Apply brings commits only: while there are any,
they are committed first — by the session's agent, asked by the frontend, or by sill for
a workspace no agent will write again. `workspaces.copy` brings them as they are.

files.description: Also the lines of each changed file, new ones counted: what a list of the changes shows.

discarded_bytes.description:
Output bytes no longer kept for replay, decimal string. Nonzero means an attach starts
partway: earlier output is gone, not lost in transit.

exit_code.description: The exit code where the daemon could see it (host terminals); none after a signal or in a jail.

Text.description: A result that is text the way the CLI prints it (`memory.show`, `memory.search`, `memory.transcript`).

command.description:
A shell call's command line as the agent declared it in the call's input, for a call of
kind `execute`; null for every other call and when the agent declared none. It is the
command itself, where `title` is display text an agent words as it likes.

purpose.description:
Why sill started the turn when the person did not: `summary` (a summary sill asked the
agent for), or a submission's `purpose` (`commit`, `crosscheck`); null for the person's own
turns and the agent's. Frontends fold a `summary` or `commit` turn to one line, and of a
`crosscheck` turn only its prompt.

Unreadable.description: A session left out of a Changes listing.

UnsupportedDetails.description:
`unsupported`: present when the method or feature needs a capability the connection did not
negotiate. Absent when the refusal is about the target (platform, policy, agent).

Upload.description:
An upload's immutable bytes. Submissions reference attachments by upload ID, so snapshots
never carry attachment data; a frontend fetches what it displays.

branch.description:
The branch the workspace's work is on: the one its HEAD names, the agent's own when it
made one.

path.description: Where the clone is on the host.

source.description: The repository as the person and the jail know it.

WorkspaceOperation.description: An operation on the workspace that stopped part way or that a restart interrupted.

state.description:
`interrupted` (its effect could not be established; shown, never redone), `conflict`,
`waiting` (a carry put off until the workspace's own work is applied or discarded) or
`notice` (a line for the person until they Apply or Discard). Apply stays offered for the
last two.

oneOf.description: Its session has not ended: it may be working in it.
Its session ended with work the person has not applied or discarded.

offered.doc: Daemon-host free space and inactive-session build-cache cleanup.
offered.name: sill.storage

offered.doc: _sill/crosscheck.*: a second opinion on a workspace's work from one Reviewer, a saved agent with its options; a submission may carry the purpose `crosscheck`.
offered.name: sill.crosscheck

offered.doc: _sill/submissions.send_now: a queued submission goes next, the active turn stopped.
offered.name: sill.send_now

offered.doc: The frontend shows session permission state: it may change session capability choices (_sill/permissions.set, apply_development, restore_defaults) and operate sessions using Desktop development or Host control capabilities.
offered.name: sill.permission_modes

offered.doc: _sill/desktop.capture and _sill/desktop.read: pictures of a session's test desktop, for a live view.
offered.name: sill.desktop_view

offered.doc: _sill/agents.discover and _sill/agents.discovered: a first start in a throwaway jail proposes an installed agent's home_paths; the person approves them on the Agents page (saved with _sill/agents.save).
offered.name: sill.agent_setup

offered.doc: _sill/workspaces.*: a session's own clone and branch of a repository; the person merges (fast-forward) or discards the result. _sill/workspaces.changed goes only to connections answered this capability.
offered.name: sill.workspaces

offered.doc: _sill/policy.quiet_host: stop showing a host's refusal banner in every session, without granting access.
offered.name: sill.network_quiet

offered.doc: _sill/usage.active_time: the time agents worked per hour, over all sessions, for a running-time chart.
offered.name: sill.usage

offered.doc: Host logins hand their pages to the frontend (`open_url` login progress) instead of opening a browser on the daemon host; _sill/streams.login_callback relays the page's loopback callback from a frontend on another machine; _sill/operations.cancel stops a running login.
offered.name: sill.login_browser

offered.doc: _sill/procs.running: what runs in a session's jail now, commands apart from services, seen from outside the agent (docs/jail-processes.md); _sill/procs.stop_command stops one command with its tree.
offered.name: sill.jail_processes

offered.doc: _sill/providers.*: model providers, records on the daemon host for OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The daemon derives the configuration, the key and the network grant of agents it has a translation for (docs/model-providers.md).
offered.name: sill.providers

offered.doc: Per-model provider token limits and Ollama active-context detection.
offered.name: sill.provider_limits

offered.doc: The frontend displays Host control: the session's caption (a line in the control's colour for as long as it is active, with its words when it starts or its scope changes) and the window-level line naming every session with active control. It may activate and revoke (_sill/host_control.activate, revoke); attached to a session, it counts as displaying that session's control, which ends when the last such connection goes.
offered.name: sill.host_control

capabilities.rules: Names are namespace.feature (lowercase ASCII, digits, '_'); versions are cumulative from 1; the daemon answers min(offered, supported) and omits unknown ones. A missing capability disables that feature only; it is never a protocol mismatch.

errors.details_rule: Codes not listed carry no details in sfp/1. Listed shapes may only gain optional fields; clients ignore unknown fields and unknown codes.
errors.retry: Unknown codes, timeouts and disconnections never authorize automatic mutation retry. Recover durable outcomes or read current state as specified by the method.

methods.doc: Read used, total and available bytes on the daemon host home and state filesystems.
methods.name: _sill/storage.space

methods.doc: Scan known session build caches; active sessions cannot be cleared.
methods.name: _sill/storage.caches

methods.doc: Detach and remove only the known build cache of an inactive session; read caches again after uncertainty before repeating.
methods.name: _sill/storage.clear_build_cache

methods.doc: Read the saved Reviewers and, for every agent that can review, the options its latest session reported.
methods.name: _sill/crosscheck.reviewers

methods.doc: Save the Reviewers. Read them after uncertainty before repeating.
methods.name: _sill/crosscheck.set_reviewers

methods.doc: Read a workspace's review, when it has one, and whether its files are still the ones reviewed.
methods.name: _sill/crosscheck.get

methods.doc: Capture the workspace's work and start a Reviewer on it, replacing the workspace's earlier review. The same operation_id answers with the review it started; never replay uncertain work under a new one.
methods.name: _sill/crosscheck.start

methods.doc: Remove a review: one under way is cancelled and its Reviewer stopped. A review already gone is not an error.
methods.name: _sill/crosscheck.remove

methods.doc: A workspace's review changed or was removed; read it again. Sent only to connections answered sill.crosscheck.
methods.name: _sill/crosscheck.changed

methods.doc: Release this connection's immutable memory text snapshot early.
methods.name: _sill/memory.text.close

methods.doc: Delete one exact session. Inspect existence after uncertainty; never replay against a replacement identity.
methods.name: _sill/sessions.delete

methods.doc: Explicitly replace a conversation generation. Never blindly retry after uncertainty.
methods.name: _sill/sessions.reset

methods.doc: Read a bounded daemon-host session log tail.
methods.name: _sill/sessions.log

methods.doc: Read daemon-host file/repository information with exact path bytes and bounded results.
methods.name: _sill/files.find

methods.doc: The repository containing the path: the nearest directory with `.git`, the path itself when it is a directory; null outside any repository.
